legal_aid.name: Contra Costa Public Defender — Clean Slate

programs.name: Probation Pretrial Services
programs.summary: Run by Contra Costa County Probation. Performs pretrial risk assessments for the court using the Public Safety Assessment (PSA) — scores for failure to appear and new criminal activity (1–6) and a violence flag — and supervises people released to pretrial. Reporting instructions are on a separate Probation page.

programs.name: Veterans Treatment Court / Military Diversion
programs.summary: For veterans whose cases are affected by service-connected issues (PTSD, TBI, substance use, mental health). Judicial supervision plus treatment, probation and a veteran mentor. VA eligibility required; some offenses excluded under PC 1170.9; judge makes final decision. Department 37, one Friday a month at 10:00 a.m.
programs.todo: Contacts are email-only on the page

programs.name: Community Homeless Court
programs.summary: Helps people with a history of homelessness clear infraction fines, giving credit for community service or other steps taken. Held at the Concord Adult Homeless Shelter.
programs.todo: Infractions only; eligibility details not on court page

jails.name: Martinez Detention Facility (MDF)
jails.phone_note: Maximum security; primary intake point for all arrestees booked in Contra Costa County; pre-sentenced and sentenced. Visiting Mon/Tue/Wed/Sat/Sun 8:30–11 a.m., 1–5 p.m., 7:30–9 p.m.; Thu 8:30–11 a.m., 1–5 p.m.; Fri 7:30–9 p.m. Up to 4 visitors, must be scheduled.
jails.todo: Sheriff's page does not state whether MDF houses men, women or both. court_ids = nearest criminal courthouses (same Martinez civic center), not confirmed.

jails.name: West County Detention Facility (WCDF)
jails.phone_note: Direct-supervision, co-educational, program-oriented campus (up to 900 on Main Campus). Visiting Mon–Thu hourly 7 a.m.–2 p.m. (no noon), Sat–Sun 7 a.m.–4 p.m.; up to 3 visitors, must be scheduled.
jails.todo: 'both' inferred from sheriff's description 'co-educational'. court_ids = nearest criminal courthouse, not confirmed.

jails.name: West County Reentry Treatment and Housing (WRTH)
jails.phone_note: Opened 2026 on the WCDF campus; up to 272 people with mental health, medical or security needs; reentry program space and clinic. Visitors check in at the WCDF lobby; same visiting blocks as WCDF.
jails.todo: Gender housed not stated. court_ids = nearest criminal courthouse, not confirmed.

jails.name: Marsh Creek Detention Facility (MCDF)
jails.phone_note: Minimum security ('the farm'); houses people already sentenced for lesser offenses; average ~70, capacity 154. Visiting Sat & Sun 1:00 and 2:00 p.m.
jails.todo: Gender housed not stated. Sentenced population, so court trips are uncommon. court_ids = nearest criminal courthouse by rough distance, not confirmed.

jails.name: John A. Davis Juvenile Hall
jails.phone_note: Probation-run, 270-bed max-security youth facility (youth up to age 25). Weekdays 8–5: 925-957-2700; after hours/weekends: 925-957-2740; special-visit scheduling 925-957-2725. Two hours of visits per week (one weekday, one weekend day).
jails.todo: Juvenile matters are heard at Walnut Creek (and some at Pittsburg); which court youth from JH attend not confirmed.

bail.note: CA Department of Insurance 'Check a License' to verify a bail agent. The court's Criminal page posts felony and misdemeanor bail schedules (2026 schedules effective 7/8/26). Inmate money (not bail) is accepted only as money orders/cashier's checks payable to 'Office of the Sheriff' with name and booking number, or by card at MDF/WCDF lobby kiosks, (866) 345-1884, or smartdeposit.com.
